summary: At our Artemis London 2026 catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities conference in September, a session focused on catastrophe bonds explored how advances in modelling can help investors further assess risk, and why managers should be cautious about encouraging investors to over-allocate to the asset class when spreads are below average. “I think particularly, if attractive spreads are becoming slightly harder to find within more familiar risks and newer perils are becoming more attractive, then the analytical bar for those new perils shouldn’t lower.” The discussion also cautioned against encouraging cat bond investors to over-allocate when spreads are below average, with DeCaro emphasising that managers should preserve credibility and capacity for when the market hardens. This second panel session of the day was titled “From hard market to normalisation: Cat bond discipline in practice.” The panel was moderated by Nils Ossenbrink , Head of Distribution and Products, Twelve Securis.

title: Americans Reject Use of AI for Medical and Coverage Decisions
title_original: Americans Reject Use of AI for Medical and Coverage Decisions
summary: Most Americans don’t want artificial intelligence making decisions about their medical care and insurance, according to a new Pew Research Center report. “They want a human in the loop doing final reviews.” Only 5% of Americans were open to insurance claim decisions being made by AI without human review, and almost half of respondents said they did not want AI to play any role these decisions, according to the report. While Americans are generally open to AI use in healthcare for tasks like translating, 60% of the 3,488 US adults Pew surveyed in June said they were uncomfortable with AI helping their doctor make a diagnosis or treatment plans.
